This is why I call string_view a "parameter-only type": it's fine to take as a parameter, but not fine to return or to store as a variable. (For sane definitions of "fine" and "not fine," of course. The blog post demonstrates one way it can go "not fine.")

https://quuxplusone.github.io/blog/2018/03/27/string-view-is...

With GCC and `-fsanitize=address,undefined` flag(s) I have catched it during runtime.

I've got a nice `==31604==ERROR: AddressSanitizer: stack-use-after-scope on address`

Oh this is nasty. But the proposed solution of making admin_id a singleton is weird.

The real fix is don't pass in a temporary to the sanitize function.

std::string_view username = Sanitize("foobarbazboo");
                                        ^- temporary std::string created here

  std::string_view Sanitize(const std::string& input) { ... }
                 ^                           ^- reference to that temporary string
                 +- returns a view to a temporary string

  std::string_view username = // possibly data freed and dangling string

> For example, this only works because the string foobarbazboo is the same length as admin_id

12 != 8
